title: Reporting with passives; it is said that...

sections.title: Reporting with passives: introduction
sections.content:
We often use a passive to report what people say, think, etc., particularly if it is not important to mention who is being reported:
• People in the area have been told that they should stay indoors.
• Everyone was asked to bring some food to the party.

sections.title: it + passive verb + that-clause
sections.content:
Another common way of reporting what is said by an unspecified group of people is to use it + passive verb + that-clause (see Unit 33 for more on that-clauses). Using this pattern allows us to put important information at the end of the sentence (see Units 22C and 22D):
• It is reported that the damage is extensive. (compare The damage is extensive, according to government sources.)
• It was decided that the meeting should be cancelled. (or It was decided to cancel the meeting.)
Also: allege, announce, assume, believe, calculate, claim, consider, demonstrate, discover, establish, estimate, expect, feel, find, know, mention, recommend, reveal, say, show, suggest, suppose, think, understand.
These verbs can also be followed by a to-infinitive clause: agree, decide, hope, intend, plan, propose.
Note that many other verbs connected with reporting are not used with it + passive verb + that-clause, but can be used as in A:
Also: encourage, persuade, reassure, remind, tell, warn.
These verbs need a personal object before the that-clause in an active form (e.g. They have informed us that …)

sections.title: subject + passive verb + to-infinitive
sections.content:
An alternative to it + passive verb + that-clause is to use subject + passive verb + to-infinitive if we want the subject to be the topic of the sentence (see Unit 22C). Compare:
• It is reported that the damage is extensive. and
• The damage is reported to be extensive.
Most of the verbs listed in the first white box in B can also be used in this pattern except for announce, decide, mention, propose, recommend, suggest.
We can only use tell in this pattern when it means 'order'. So we can say:
• I was told (= ordered) to go with them to the railway station.
but not 'The accident was told (= said) to have happened just after midnight'.

sections.title: it + passive verb + wh-clause
sections.content:
With some verbs we can also use it + passive verb + wh-clause to report information given or found out:
• It has now been revealed who was responsible for the accident.
• The decision to build the bridge was taken before it was established whether it was actually needed.
Also: discover, explain, find, know, reveal, show, understand.

sections.title: there + passive verb + to be
sections.content:
When a that-clause begins that + there ..., we can make a corresponding passive form there + passive verb + to be (present) / to have been (past). Compare:
• It is thought (that) there are / were too many obstacles to peace. and
• There are thought to be / to have been too many obstacles to peace.
We can use the same verbs in this pattern as with subject + passive verb + to-infinitive (see C).

exercises.question: It was ___ to hold new negotiations next month.
exercises.hint: Both agree and announce can be used with it + passive + to-infinitive clause.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Both announced and agreed
Both agree and announce can be used with it + passive + to-infinitive clause. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.question: It has been ___ that the crash was the result of pilot error.
exercises.hint: Show and reveal are both possible here.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Both shown and revealed
Show and reveal are both possible here.

exercises.question: It was ___ that Mrs Ho would chair the meeting.
exercises.hint: Hope and reveal are both possible; explain is not used in Pattern 1.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Both hoped and revealed
Hope and reveal are both possible; explain is not used in Pattern 1.

exercises.question: It has been ___ to appoint Dr Ahmadi as head teacher.
exercises.hint: Decide and propose can be followed by a to-infinitive clause.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Both decided and proposed
Decide and propose can be followed by a to-infinitive clause. This verb pattern requires a to-infinitive as its complement.

exercises.question: It has now been ___ that half of cancer cases are lifestyle-related.
exercises.hint: Reveal, establish, and discover all work for Pattern 1.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: All of these
Reveal, establish, and discover all work for Pattern 1. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: It is ___ that another moon landing will take place next year.
exercises.hint: Assume, thought, and expect all work for Pattern 1.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: All of these
Assume, thought, and expect all work for Pattern 1. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: AGREEMENT THAT UN WILL SEND IN TROOPS (newspaper headline)
options: It has been agreed that the UN will send in troops.
The UN is agreed to send in troops.
UN will send in troops was agreed.
exercises.hint: Pattern 1 (it was agreed that...) is suitable for this headline.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: It has been agreed that the UN will send in troops.
Pattern 1 (it was agreed that...) is suitable for this headline. The present perfect links past events to the present. The key signals are: just, already, yet, ever, never, since, for, recently, and incomplete time expressions like this week or today (when not yet over).

exercises.question: TERRORISTS BELIEVED TO BE OPERATING IN BERLIN
exercises.answer: Terrorists are believed to be operating in Berlin.
exercises.hint: Both Pattern 1 (it is believed that) and Pattern 2 (terrorists are believed to be) are possible.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Both are possible.
Both Pattern 1 (it is believed that) and Pattern 2 (terrorists are believed to be) are possible.

exercises.question: WARNING GIVEN ABOUT COMPUTER VIRUS
options: It is warned about computer viruses.
It has been warned that computer viruses exist.
exercises.hint: Pattern 1: it is warned that... (warn is not in the list for Pattern 1 but it can be used with personal object in active, and here it works as it-clause).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: It is warned about computer viruses.
Pattern 1: it is warned that... (warn is not in the list for Pattern 1 but it can be used with personal object in active, and here it works as it-clause).

exercises.question: It has been discovered that a mechanical fault caused the problem. / (Rewrite with Pattern 2)
options: A mechanical fault was discovered to have caused the problem.
A mechanical fault has been discovered to cause the problem.
A mechanical fault was discovered causing the problem.
exercises.hint: Pattern 2: subject + passive + to have + past participle (for past action).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: A mechanical fault was discovered to have caused the problem.
Pattern 2: subject + passive + to have + past participle (for past action). The present perfect links past events to the present. The key signals are: just, already, yet, ever, never, since, for, recently, and incomplete time expressions like this week or today (when not yet over).

exercises.question: It is not thought that the fault is serious. / (Rewrite with Pattern 2)
options: The fault is not thought to be serious.
The fault is not thought being serious.
The fault is not thought serious.
exercises.hint: Pattern 2: subject + passive + to be + adjective.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: The fault is not thought to be serious.
Pattern 2: subject + passive + to be + adjective. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: It has been decided to postpone the next rocket launch. / (Is Pattern 2 possible?)
options: No, Pattern 2 is not possible for decide.
Yes, The next rocket launch has been decided to be postponed.
Yes, To postpone the next rocket launch was decided.
Pattern 2 is possible only with person subjects.
exercises.hint: Decide is not used in Pattern 2 (subject + passive + to-infinitive).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: No, Pattern 2 is not possible for decide.
Decide is not used in Pattern 2 (subject + passive + to-infinitive). Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.sentence: He is believed that he committed the fraud over a period of five years.
exercises.correction: He is believed to have committed the fraud over a period of five years.
exercises.hint: Personal passive: He is believed TO HAVE + past participle (not 'that he').
exercises.explanation:
Answer: He is believed to have committed
There are two structures: (1) 'It is believed that he committed...' — impersonal. (2) 'He is believed to have committed...' — personal passive. These are interchangeable but you CANNOT mix them: 'He is believed that he...' is always wrong.

exercises.sentence: It is reported that the prime minister will resign imminently.
exercises.correction: It is reported that the prime minister will resign imminently.
acceptable: It is reported that the prime minister will resign imminently.
exercises.hint: 'It is reported that + clause' is correct — this is the impersonal passive structure.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: CORRECT — It is reported that the prime minister will resign imminently
'It is reported/said/believed/alleged + that-clause' is a standard impersonal passive construction. It is used extensively in journalism and formal writing to report information without attributing it to a specific source.
exercises.prompt: Is this sentence correct? If not, rewrite it correctly.

exercises.question: ___ that the company has been mismanaging its finances for years. (It / say)
exercises.hint: Impersonal passive: It + is/has been + said/reported/believed + that.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: It is said
The impersonal passive 'it is said/reported/believed/alleged/thought + that' is used to report information whose source is general or unspecified. 'It is said' = people say / it is generally said. The alternative personal passive would be: 'The company is said to have been mismanaging...'
